title: Building your first deck
goal: Know the deck-building rules and what a healthy deck looks like.

steps.html:
The rules for a legal deck:

  • Exactly 1 Leader.
  • Exactly 50 cards in the deck (Characters, Events, Stages).
  • Every card must match a Color on your Leader.
  • At most 4 copies of the same Card number.
  • Plus 10 DON!!.

Which cards are allowed in tournaments? Most events use the Standard format. Each card has a block number printed in its lower-right corner. From April 2026 to March 2027, Standard allows Blocks 2 to 5. Block 1 cards (the oldest ones) are not allowed. Each spring the oldest block rotates out (Block rotation).

What a healthy deck usually has:

  • A spread of costs: plenty of 1 to 5 cost cards, a few big 6+ cost finishers.
  • Lots of Counter cards. Most good decks have around 15 to 20 cards with +1000 or +2000 Counters, so your hand can defend you.
  • 4 copies of the cards your Leader wants most, so you find them every game.

The easiest start is a starter deck: a ready-to-play 50-card deck with a Leader. Play it a few times, then swap in cards one at a time. Check the Cards tab to see what each card does and what it costs on TCGplayer.

quiz.q: Your Leader is red and green. Can you put a blue card in your deck?
choices: No, cards must match your Leader's colors
quiz.why: Every card must share a color with your Leader.

quiz.q: How many copies of the same card number can a deck have?
quiz.why: Up to 4 copies of each card number.

quiz.q: Why do good decks run many Counter cards?
choices: They let your hand defend against attacks
They are required by the rules
quiz.why: Counters in hand are how you survive your opponent's turn.
